Any rep could make this same error, and the $1,100-on-$110 refund three weeks earlier shows it has already happened once without a system fix.

It also doesn't rely on any one person catching their own mistake.

Sam's prior incident was never followed up, and that gap deserves its own review, such as a coaching conversation or a check on Sam's refund volume. That is a separate question from which control to build, and it doesn't justify removing access when a tool change fixes the failure at its source.
